label: Quit vaping January 2027
h1: Quit vaping in January: a 30-day calendar plan

items.b:
Day 1 of 30.

Pick your reasons. Write 3 reasons you're quitting and put them in your phone's notes.

Day 2 of 30.

Spot your triggers. Each time you vape today, note what you were doing just before.

Day 3 of 30.

Tell one person. Quitting with someone in the loop is easier than quitting in secret.

Day 4 of 30.

Plan a replacement for your #1 trigger: gum, a walk, cold water or a different route home.

Day 5 of 30.

Clear the house. Remove spare pods and devices from your bag, car and drawers.

Day 6 of 30.

Quit day. Cravings typically peak and pass within a few minutes. Ride them out with a 5-minute task.

Day 7 of 30.

Expect irritability. It's withdrawal, not your personality, and it tends to ease over the next couple of weeks.

Day 8 of 30.

Drink water and move. A short walk is one of the best-studied ways to blunt a craving.

Day 9 of 30.

Change one routine that's tied to vaping (where you take breaks, what you do after meals).

Day 10 of 30.

Sleep may be off for a few days. Keep a regular bedtime and go easy on caffeine late in the day.

Day 11 of 30.

Count the money you haven't spent so far. Put it somewhere you can see it.

Day 12 of 30.

Feeling a slip coming? Delay 10 minutes, then decide. Usually the urge has moved on.

Day 13 of 30.

If you slip, it's one slip, not a relapse. Note the trigger and carry on with the plan.

Day 14 of 30.

Halfway through week two. Notice anything better: taste, breath, sleep, money?

Day 15 of 30.

Say no out loud to an offer today. Practise the line: 'No thanks, I've quit.'

Day 16 of 30.

Look at your trigger list. Which ones are already weaker?

Day 17 of 30.

Plan for your next stressful event. What will you do instead?

Day 18 of 30.

Reward yourself with something you've been saving for.

Day 19 of 30.

Free support exists. In the U.S., 1-800-QUIT-NOW connects you to your state quitline, and smokefree.gov has text programs for young people and adults.

Day 20 of 30.

Three weeks in. Write a note to yourself on day 1 describing how today feels.

Day 21 of 30.

Review your 3 reasons. Add one you've discovered since quitting.

Day 22 of 30.

Social situations: plan an exit line and something to do with your hands.

Day 23 of 30.

Check in on sleep, mood and appetite. Most people find they settle by now.

Day 24 of 30.

Clean your space: car, bag, room. Remove the last cues.

Day 25 of 30.

If cravings are still strong, ask a pharmacist or doctor about evidence-based support.

Day 26 of 30.

Think about who could use your help quitting next.

Day 27 of 30.

Plan the next 30 days. Which triggers still need a plan?

Day 28 of 30.

Celebrate four weeks with someone who supported you.

Day 29 of 30.

Write your relapse plan: what you'll do if a craving catches you off guard.

Day 30 of 30.

Day 30. You've done the hardest part. Keep the reasons list for the days you'll need it.
